extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and aesthetics; artists and critics interested in theory of taste and genius
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and applying Kant's criteria for judging and producing beautiful art, distinguishing taste from genius, and the faculties and standards that make art beautiful. Useful for philosophical analysis, art criticism, and theory-informed creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Taste and Genius
rubrics_metrics.description: For judging beautiful objects as such, taste is requisite; but for the production of beautiful art, genius is requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste is a faculty of judgement (corrected by examples from art and nature) while genius is the productive talent for creating aesthetical Ideas. This distinction underlies evaluation: one needs taste to judge beauty, but genius to create it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgement of natural vs. artificial beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural beauty pleases by mere form without a concept of purpose; artificial beauty (product of art) requires a prior concept of what the object is to be (a purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging artificial beauty one must consider the object's purposiveness and perfection with respect to its intended purpose; judging natural beauty as such requires no concept of purpose. If purposiveness is brought in for natural objects (e.g., human form), the judgement becomes teleological, not purely aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of perfection relative to purpose for artificial beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: In judging artificial beauty the perfection of the thing with respect to its inner destination (purpose) must be taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artificial beauty demands assessment of how well the manifold elements of the work accord with the intended concept or purpose; failure to do so neglects a central condition of aesthetic judgement for art-objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of ugliness: exclude disgust
rubrics_metrics.description: Art may represent ugly or calamitous things (Furies, disease, war) as beautiful, except those forms of ugliness that excite disgust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disgust is an imaginative sensation in which the object seems to obtrude itself and thereby destroys all aesthetic satisfaction. Artistic representation of disgust cannot be beautiful; sculpture circumvents this by allegory or pleasing attributes rather than literal repulsive depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of Taste in production and refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste is the faculty by which artists check and correct their work; it is exercised and refined by manifold examples from art or nature and turns effort into satisfying form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste is disciplinary, not productive: the artist refines and polishes imaginative material through taste. Works produced strictly by rule or mechanical skill may have pleasing form but are not works of beautiful art in the full sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of genius as faculty for aesthetical Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius is the talent for producing aesthetical Ideas: representations of the imagination that provoke abundant thought but cannot be fully captured by definite concepts or language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic Ideas are creative, striving beyond empirical experience and approximating rational Ideas. Genius brings such Ideas into expression; it is not learnable by science or mere industry but is a natural gift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aesthetical Idea as criterion of spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: An aesthetical Idea is a representation of the Imagination which occasions much thought without any definite concept being adequate to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Ideas enliven the mind by opening a prospect into an illimitable field of kindred representations. Examples (poetic lines) illustrate how an attribute quickens a rational Idea beyond conceptual limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constituents of genius: Imagination and Understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius consists in the happy relation between Imagination (productive, free) and Understanding (which supplies a concept/purpose), enabling Ideas to be found for a concept and expressed so others can share the subjective state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relation cannot be taught; genius requires both free imaginative fecundity and conformity to conceptual law so that imagination's abundance is purposive rather than lawless nonsense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression (spirit) as necessary faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond generating aesthetical Ideas, the artist must have the faculty to seize the fleeting play of imagination and unify it in an expression that communicates the ineffable element (this faculty is called spirit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spirit is the animating principle that renders the subjective state occasioned by aesthetic Ideas communicable—through language, painting, music, etc.—and thus essential to beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius yields exemplary originality, not rules for imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The product of genius is an example that awakens originality in other geniuses and yields new rules for art; it is not meant to be imitated literally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genius's example can found a school (teachable rules derived from peculiar products), but literal copying removes what is specifically genius and reduces the work to mere manner or aping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aping and mannerism are faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Aping (copying every deformity) and mannerism ( ostentatious peculiarities ) are defects: imitation that copies a genius's singularities without possessing exemplary talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mannerism arises when exposition is founded on singularity rather than on appropriateness to the Idea; affected behaviour betrays a bungler. Imitation should follow the spirit of an exemplary work, not its idiosyncratic faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of Judgement (Taste) over Genius when conflict arises
rubrics_metrics.description: In art the Judgement (taste) is the indispensable condition of beauty and, if conflict between imagination and judgement occurs, the freedom and abundance of imagination should be sacrificed rather than the clarity and lawfulness demanded by understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abundance of Ideas without conformity to law leads to nonsense. Taste disciplines genius, bringing clearness and universal communicability to imaginative wealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four requisites for beautiful art
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagination, Understanding, Spirit, and Taste are all requisite for beautiful art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each faculty plays a role: Imagination supplies Ideas; Understanding supplies the concept/purpose; Spirit animates expression; Taste disciplines form so it becomes universally communicable and enduring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful art: purposiveness without purpose (formal purposiveness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful art should present purposiveness in form relative to our judgement while remaining free from a determinate purpose (i.e., purposive for aesthetic contemplation but not utilitarian purpose).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art is not like tradesman's work with measurable standards; it must appear free and self-contained. If an artwork appears studied or anxious toward external ends, it ceases to be beautiful art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of the beautiful arts by mode of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The arts divide analogically into three kinds of expression: by word (speech: rhetoric and poetry), deportment (formative arts: plastic and painting), and tone (play of sensations: music, art of colour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This taxonomy links medium to how thought, intuition, and sensation are communicated. Each class has distinct criteria (e.g., poetry combines free imagination with conceptual food for the understanding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria distinguishing rhetoric and poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhetoric is the art of carrying on serious business of the Understanding as if it were a free play; poetry conducts free play of the Imagination as if it were serious business of Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The orator promises serious instruction but often supplies entertainment; the poet promises entertainment but supplies substance for understanding. Beware rhetoric-as-deception (persuasion that usurps judgement), which is inappropriate for law courts or pulpit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction within formative arts: plastic (sculpture, architecture) vs painting
rubrics_metrics.description: Plastic arts (sculpture, architecture) present figures cognisable corporeally (sight and touch) and may express concepts as if they existed in nature; painting presents sensible illusion and arrangement of appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architecture has use/purpose as determining ground (suitability for use), whereas sculpture aims at pure expression of aesthetical Ideas. Landscape gardening is a formative art of arranging products of nature (appearance of utility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Art of the beautiful play of sensations (music and colour)
rubrics_metrics.description: This art concerns the proportion and tone of sensory dispositions (hearing and sight). Whether colours/tones are mere pleasant sensations or constitute beauty depends on judgement and possibly an intelligible (mathematical) element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music may be treated as beautiful art (a play of sensations judged by form/proportion) rather than merely a source of pleasant feeling; perceptual limits complicate immediate judgement of tones and colours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of arts and the role of moral (self-sufficing) Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining arts (e.g., opera: poetry+music+theatre) may make art more artistic; but only combination with moral Ideas yields self-sufficing satisfaction—without moral ideas the arts risk becoming mere distraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple satisfactions can cross and sometimes diminish beauty. If arts serve only to distract and increase discontent, they fail their higher end; early habituation to natural beauty is beneficial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative aesthetic worth: poetry's primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry ranks highest among the arts because it best expands the mind by setting imagination at liberty and aesthetically rising to Ideas, supplying conceptual nourishment via imaginative play.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhetoric (as persuasion) is dialectic and potentially deceptive; poetry declares itself play and so preserves honesty. The energy of poetry makes it most conducive to genuine aesthetic and intellectual enrichment.
